page.name: Education & training
page.metaDescription: Enrollment confirmations, schedule changes, deadline reminders and attendance notices over the messaging accounts your institution already holds.
page.lede: Education messaging is about timing: a class that moved, a deadline that is close, an enrollment nobody confirmed. The failure mode is not a missing message — it is one that arrives after it mattered.

sections.h: What your institution sends each term
bullets: Event and term-start reminders to a cohort

sections.h: Send to a whole cohort without tripping a limit
p: Sending to a whole cohort at once is a burst, and providers apply a limit per sender number. The platform spreads a batch to that limit rather than failing partway through, and the pacing is visible in the console so a term-start send does not quietly become a two-hour job.
bullets: Batch and scheduled sends spread to the provider limit per number
Bulk and scheduled behavior documented in the help center
Opt-out suppression applied to promotional sends, not to transactional ones

sections.h: Who may be contacted is your call
p: Guardian consent, age-related rules and institutional policy decide who can be messaged. The platform applies the rules you configure — it carries out that judgment rather than making it for you.

faq.q: Can one campaign go out to several thousand people at once?
faq.a: You can submit a batch, and the platform paces it to what your provider allows per number. Throughput rises with the number of connected sender numbers or accounts, not by overriding the provider limit.

faq.q: Can a scheduled send be canceled?
faq.a: Scheduled and bulk sending is a console feature; the exact behavior is documented in the help center rather than assumed here.

faq.q: Do you support more than one language in a message?
faq.a: Content is whatever you put in the request, so any language your provider supports can be sent. Note that non-Latin scripts change how a message is split into segments, which affects cost.
